drivingQuestion: What does 'forever' in the mishna teach?

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי לְעוֹלָם? מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: מִידֵּי דַּהֲוָה אַמִּצְרִי וַאֲדוֹמִי, מָה לְהַלָּן לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת, אַף כָּאן נָמֵי לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «What» is the meaning of the statement that the daughter of a ḥalal is unfit «forever?» The Gemara explains: It is necessary «lest you say» that the halakha should be «just as it is in» the case of «an Egyptian» convert «and an Edomite» convert, and that «just as there,» with regard to an Egyptian and an Edomite, their descendants are permitted to enter into the congregation «after three generations, so too here,» the daughter of a descendant of a ḥalal should «also» be allowed to marry into the priesthood «after three generations.» The mishna therefore «teaches us» that this prohibition is permanent.

moves.summary: One might have compared it to Egyptian and Edomite converts, permitted after three generations
moves.about: 'forever' excludes an analogy to Egyptian and Edomite converts permitted after three generations

moves.summary: The mishna teaches the taint is permanent
